rounds.text: I Power Solutions India Ltd trades at a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.45x, underpinned by a book value of ₹ 9.19 against a share price of ₹ 13.3 [E1]. The company is virtually debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x as of September 2026, successfully reducing its borrowings and maintaining flat obligations at Rs 0.04 Cr [E21, E22, E29, E30]. Long-term performance reflects positive compounding, delivering a 27% share price growth over five years and a 14% growth over a decade [E8, E9]. Furthermore, the Information Technology sector provides a neutral macro tailwind with a score of +0.45 [E39]. Conceded: the company exhibits negative return on equity at -32.7% and a sharp 59% drop in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E6, E7].

I Power Solutions India Ltd presents a severely deteriorating operational profile, highlighted by an abysmal Return on Equity of -32.7% and a deeply negative ROCE of -24.6% [E5, E6]. This value-destroying performance is structural rather than temporary, evidenced by a worsening median ROE trajectory that drops from -6% over 10 years to -33% over the last year [E12, E15]. Fundamental weakness is further underscored by a sharp -59% contraction in compounded trailing twelve-month profit growth alongside negative operating and free cash flows of -2.41 Cr and -0.34 Cr respectively for Mar 2026 [E7, E19, E20]. Compounding these operational alarms, insiders have steadily retreated, with promoter holdings dropping by 15.16 percentage points from 61.68% in Dec 2023 to 46.52% in Sep 2026 [E24]. Consequently, the rules-based screen issues a SELL verdict with a score of 42 out of 100, driven by collapsing net profits and severe decelerating earnings [E34, E35, E36]. conceded: [E1] and [E21].

Conceded: [E5], [E6], [E7], [E12], [E15], [E19], [E20], [E24], [E35], and [E36]. While the bear highlights severe operational contraction and insider reduction, these headwinds are offset by a pristine balance sheet where the company is virtually debt-free with a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x and total borrowings of just Rs 0.04 Cr [E21, E22, E30]. Furthermore, this conservative financing structure has helped insulate the firm's historical trajectory, supporting a positive 5-year compounded share price growth of 27% [E9]. The valuation of 1.45x price-to-book on a ₹ 9.19 book value correctly prices in these operational turnarounds without demanding an excessive multiple [E1], while sector tailwinds maintain a neutral backdrop for Information Technology [E39]. Finally, the bias check confirms that no major valuation, momentum, or macro red-flags invalidate the structural setup [E38].

Conceded: [E21], [E22], [E30], and [E39]. While the balance sheet is virtually debt-free with borrowings at just Rs 0.04 Cr and sector tailwinds read neutral, a clean debt profile does nothing to generate earnings when operations are actively contracting [E21, E22, E30, E39]. The bull's reliance on a 5-year compounded share price growth of 27% ignores that momentum has collapsed over the short term, with 1-year share price growth plunging by -38% and the stock languishing at just 6% of its 52-week range [E4, E9, E11]. Furthermore, pointing to a price-to-book ratio of 1.45x ignores the deteriorating underlying quality, given that ROE has steadily worsened to -32.7%, ROCE sits at -24.6%, and 10-year, 5-year, and 3-year median ROEs are all deeply negative [E1, E5, E6, E12, E13, E14]. The operational reality is severe cash burn, evidenced by a negative operating cash flow of Rs -2.41 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -0.34 Cr in Mar 2026, which makes the bull's valuation defense untenable [E19, E20]. Finally, insiders are signaling a clear lack of confidence as promoter holdings have dropped by 15.16 percentage points down to 46.52% [E24].
